title: Boss: INC-4107, orders missing after a broker failover
summary: Audit topic durability, find the hot consumer, explain where every group restarted, and prove the commit order that loses nothing.

steps.title: INC-4107: orders missing in billing after a broker failover
body: **INC-4107** Â· Sev 2 Â· Service: billing Â· Reporter: finance operations
> Since last night's patch window, 37 orders are **paid in the shop but never invoiced**. The new `fraud-check`
> service, deployed the same night, has **seen no orders at all**. The billing lag alert has fired twice since.
02:03  broker kafka-1 restarted (kernel patch), leadership of orders-* moved to kafka-2
02:15  billing restarted with auto.offset.reset=earliest after being stopped for 3 days (orders keeps 48 hours)
02:40  ALERT ConsumerLagHigh billing/orders: 49535 (billing-2 removed by the autoscaler)
1. A durability audit flags every risky topic and producer setting (step 1).
2. We know which billing member carries the lag after the scale-down (step 2).
3. For every partition we can say where each group restarted and how many records retention deleted (step 3).
4. A simulation proves which commit order loses orders and which one duplicates them, and that the inbox fixes

steps.title: 1. Durability audit
prompt: Write `List<string> Audit(List<TopicSetup> topics)`. The record is given (do not declare it):
`record TopicSetup(string Name, int Replicas, int MinInsync, string Acks, bool Idempotent, bool UncleanElection);`
For each topic, in input order, add every finding that applies, in this order:
1. `Replicas < 3` â†’ `"{name}: replication factor {r} (use 3)"`
2. `MinInsync >= Replicas` â†’ `"{name}: min.insync.replicas {m} >= replication factor {r}: one broker down blocks acks=all writes"`
3. `MinInsync < 2` â†’ `"{name}: min.insync.replicas {m}: a single replica can acknowledge"`
4. `Acks != "all"` â†’ `"{name}: acks={acks} can lose acknowledged writes"`
5. not idempotent â†’ `"{name}: idempotence off: retries can duplicate"`
6. unclean election on â†’ `"{name}: unclean.leader.election.enable=true can lose committed writes"`
A healthy topic adds nothing.
solution: if (t.MinInsync >= t.Replicas) f.Add($"{t.Name}: min.insync.replicas {t.MinInsync} >= replication factor {t.Replicas}: one broker down blocks acks=all writes");
if (t.MinInsync < 2) f.Add($"{t.Name}: min.insync.replicas {t.MinInsync}: a single replica can acknowledge");
if (t.Acks != "all") f.Add($"{t.Name}: acks={t.Acks} can lose acknowledged writes");
if (!t.Idempotent) f.Add($"{t.Name}: idempotence off: retries can duplicate");
if (t.UncleanElection) f.Add($"{t.Name}: unclean.leader.election.enable=true can lose committed writes");
hints: Six independent `if` statements per topic, in the listed order (not `else if`: one topic can break several rules).
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("the orders topic from the incident", new List<string>
"orders: min.insync.replicas 1: a single replica can acknowledge",
"orders: acks=1 can lose acknowledged writes",
"orders: idempotence off: retries can duplicate",
}, Audit(new List<TopicSetup> { new("orders", 3, 1, "1", false, false) }));
Dojo.Eq("too strict to write", new List<string>
"payments: min.insync.replicas 3 >= replication factor 3: one broker down blocks acks=all writes",
}, Audit(new List<TopicSetup> { new("payments", 3, 3, "all", true, false) }));
Dojo.Eq("a healthy topic adds nothing", new List<string>(), Audit(new List<TopicSetup> { new("shipments", 3, 2, "all", true, false) }));
Dojo.Eq("several topics keep input order", new List<string>
"audit: replication factor 1 (use 3)",
"audit: min.insync.replicas 1 >= replication factor 1: one broker down blocks acks=all writes",
"audit: min.insync.replicas 1: a single replica can acknowledge",
"audit: unclean.leader.election.enable=true can lose committed writes",
"events: acks=0 can lose acknowledged writes",
}, Audit(new List<TopicSetup> { new("audit", 1, 1, "all", true, true), new("shipments", 3, 2, "all", true, false), new("events", 3, 2, "0", true, false) }));
record TopicSetup(string Name, int Replicas, int MinInsync, string Acks, bool Idempotent, bool UncleanElection);

steps.title: 2. Who carries the lag after the scale-down
prompt: billing uses the **range** assignor. After the autoscaler removed `billing-2`, find the member that now owns the most lag.
Write `string Hottest(List<string> members, int partitions, Dictionary<int, long> lag)`:
- assign with the range rule: members sorted by name (ordinal), `partitions / n` consecutive partitions each, one extra
for the first `partitions % n` members;
- sum each member's lag (`lag` may lack a partition: count it as 0);
- return the member with the largest sum (the first in sorted order on a tie) as
`"{member}: lag {sum} on [{its partitions joined with ','}]"`;
- no members â†’ `"no members"`.
starter: string Hottest(List<string> members, int partitions, Dictionary<int, long> lag)
solution: string Hottest(List<string> members, int partitions, Dictionary<int, long> lag)
int per = partitions / sorted.Count, extra = partitions % sorted.Count, next = 0;
hints: Reuse the range rule from the lesson, then `parts.Sum(p => lag.GetValueOrDefault(p))`.
Track the best with a strict `>` so the first member wins a tie.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("after billing-2 left", "billing-3: lag 49535 on [3,4,5]", Hottest(new List<string> { "billing-3", "billing-1" }, 6, dojoLag));
Dojo.Eq("uneven split", "b: lag 10 on [3,4]", Hottest(new List<string> { "c", "a", "b" }, 7, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 1, [1] = 1, [2] = 1, [3] = 5, [4] = 5 }));
Dojo.Eq("idle members carry nothing", "b: lag 9 on [1]", Hottest(new List<string> { "a", "b", "c", "d" }, 2, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 5, [1] = 9 }));
Dojo.Eq("a tie goes to the first member", "x: lag 4 on [0]", Hottest(new List<string> { "y", "x" }, 2, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 4, [1] = 4 }));
Dojo.Eq("no members", "no members", Hottest(new List<string>(), 6, dojoLag));

steps.title: 3. Where did every group restart?
prompt: Explain, per partition, where a group starts after the night's restarts.
Write `List<string> StartReport(Dictionary<int, long?> committed, Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string reset)`.
For every partition in `logEnd`, ascending:
- a committed offset inside `[logStart, logEnd]` â†’ `"p{n}: {offset} committed"`;
- otherwise the start comes from `reset` (`"earliest"` â†’ log start, `"latest"` â†’ log end), with the reason:
- no committed offset (missing or `null`) â†’ `"p{n}: {start} reset to {reset} (no committed offset)"`
- below the log start â†’ `"p{n}: {start} reset to {reset} (committed {c} below log start {s}: {s - c} records lost to retention)"`
- beyond the log end â†’ `"p{n}: {start} reset to {reset} (committed {c} beyond log end {e})"`
- any other `reset` value with an invalid offset â†’ throw `InvalidOperationException`.
starter: List<string> StartReport(Dictionary<int, long?> committed, Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string reset)
solution: List<string> StartReport(Dictionary<int, long?> committed, Dictionary<int, long> logStart, Dictionary<int, long> logEnd, string reset)
if (c is long v && v >= s && v <= e)
var reason = c is null ? "no committed offset"
: c < s ? $"committed {c} below log start {s}: {s - c} records lost to retention"
hints: Pick the reason first, then the start offset with a `switch` that throws for unknown policies.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoStart = new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 1000, [1] = 900, [2] = 1500 };
var dojoEnd = new Dictionary<int, long> { [2] = 7000, [0] = 5000, [1] = 6000 };
Dojo.Eq("billing after 3 days off", new List<string>
"p0: 4200 committed",
"p1: 900 reset to earliest (committed 300 below log start 900: 600 records lost to retention)",
"p2: 1500 reset to earliest (committed 8000 beyond log end 7000)",
}, StartReport(new Dictionary<int, long?> { [0] = 4200, [1] = 300, [2] = 8000 }, dojoStart, dojoEnd, "earliest"));
Dojo.Eq("fraud-check on its first start", new List<string>
"p0: 5000 reset to latest (no committed offset)",
"p1: 6000 reset to latest (no committed offset)",
"p2: 7000 reset to latest (no committed offset)",
}, StartReport(new Dictionary<int, long?>(), dojoStart, dojoEnd, "latest"));
Dojo.Eq("a null commit counts as none", new List<string> { "p0: 1000 reset to earliest (no committed offset)" },
StartReport(new Dictionary<int, long?> { [0] = null }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 1000 }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 5000 }, "earliest"));
Dojo.Eq("none is fine while every offset is valid", new List<string> { "p0: 1200 committed" },
StartReport(new Dictionary<int, long?> { [0] = 1200 }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 1000 }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 5000 }, "none"));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("none refuses an invalid offset", () =>
StartReport(new Dictionary<int, long?> { [0] = 10 }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 1000 }, new Dictionary<int, long> { [0] = 5000 }, "none"));

steps.title: 4. Commit order: prove it
prompt: billing committed **before** handling (`consumer.Commit(cr); Handle(cr);`). Prove what each commit order does across one crash.
Write `List<string> Run(string[] log, int crashAt, string mode)`. The consumer reads one partition from offset 0 and
commits after every record. It crashes **once**, at offset `crashAt`, exactly between its two actions for that
record, then restarts from the committed offset and runs to the end without crashing again. Return the values the
handler processed, in order. Modes:
- `"commit-first"`: commit `offset + 1`, then handle. The crash comes after the commit, before the handling.
- `"commit-after"`: handle, then commit `offset + 1`. The crash comes after the handling, before the commit.
- `"commit-after+dedup"`: like `commit-after`, but the handler first checks an **inbox** of processed offsets (it lives
in the database, so it survives the crash) and skips an offset it has already processed.
- any other mode â†’ throw `ArgumentException`.
A `crashAt` beyond the log means no crash.
starter: List<string> Run(string[] log, int crashAt, string mode)
solution: List<string> Run(string[] log, int crashAt, string mode)
if (crashHere) { crashed = true; pos = committed; continue; }
if (crashHere) { crashed = true; pos = committed; continue; }
hints: Loop with a position `pos`; on the crash set `pos = committed` and `continue` instead of moving on.
In `commit-first` the commit happens before the crash check; in the other modes the handling does.
`inbox.Add(o)` returns false when the offset is already there: use it as the dedup check.
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoLog = new[] { "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4" };
Dojo.Eq("commit first: A3 is lost (INC-4107)", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 2, "commit-first"));
Dojo.Eq("commit after: A3 is processed twice", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A3", "A3", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 2, "commit-after"));
Dojo.Eq("commit after + inbox: exactly one effect each", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 2, "commit-after+dedup"));
Dojo.Eq("no crash", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 99, "commit-after"));
Dojo.Eq("commit first, crash on the first record", new List<string> { "A2", "A3", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 0, "commit-first"));
Dojo.Eq("commit after, crash on the last record", new List<string> { "A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A4" }, Run(dojoLog, 3, "commit-after"));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("unknown mode", () => Run(dojoLog, 0, "auto"));
